Maximum likelihood estimation of \(\theta\) based on Ewens sampling formula

Source: R/estimation.R
optim_ewens.Rd

optim_ewens() computes the maximum likelihood estimate of Ewens \(\theta\) parameter for a given species abundance distribution \((n_1, ..., n_k)\) where \(n_i\) is the number of organisms of species i in the sample and k is the total number of species in the sample (for all \(i, n_i > 0\)). The input should be a vector; species with zero abundance are ignored.

The maximum likelihood estimate is the root of \(k = \theta[\psi(\theta+J)-\psi(\theta)]\) (the expected number of species equals the observed one), where \(\psi\) is the digamma function and \(J=\sum n_i\). It is found by a one-dimensional root search to full numerical precision, so no general-purpose optimiser is involved.

Usage

optim_ewens(input_abundances)

Arguments

input_abundances

a vector of integers (species abundances)

Value

A list with

theta

the \(\theta\) parameter of Ewens sampling formula, a real value

logl

the maximal value of the log-likelihood (see Details), a real value; it is comparable with the logl value of optim_pitman()

Boundary cases

The likelihood function has no interior maximum when all individuals belong to a single species (k = 1, the estimate is theta = 0) or when every species has a single individual (k = J, the estimate is theta = Inf). A warning is issued and the boundary value is returned.

Log-likelihood

logl is the log-probability of the partition (the exchangeable partition probability function of Ewens sampling formula). Terms that depend on the data only, and not on the model, are omitted. It is on the same scale as the logl returned by optim_pitman(). Note that the Ewens model is equal to the Pitman model when \(\sigma = 0\), so the two models are nested and can be compared directly, for instance with the likelihood-ratio statistic \(2(\mathrm{logl}_{Pitman} - \mathrm{logl}_{Ewens})\) or with AIC.

See also

optim_pitman(), optim_multideme()

Examples

input_abundances <- c(234, 87, 34, 5, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1)
optim_ewens(input_abundances)
#> $theta
#> [1] 2.476993
#> 
#> $logl
#> [1] -433.6187
#>
